import pandas as pd

def main():
    # List all source file paths
    source_files = [
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_59/test_0.csv"
        # If there were more sources, add them here, e.g.
        # "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_59/test_1.csv",
        # "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_59/test_2.csv",
        # ...
    ]

    # Initialize an empty list to hold dataframes
    dfs = []

    # Load each source file, extract needed columns, and append to dfs list
    for file_path in source_files:
        df = pd.read_csv(file_path)
        # Extract only the columns needed for the target schema
        # Target schema: ['PRODUCTLINE': string, 'SALES': float]
        # The source has these columns, so just select them
        df_subset = df[['PRODUCTLINE', 'SALES']].copy()
        dfs.append(df_subset)

    # Concatenate all dataframes vertically
    combined_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

    # Group by PRODUCTLINE and sum SALES to match target examples style
    result_df = combined_df.groupby('PRODUCTLINE', as_index=False)['SALES'].sum()

    # Sort by PRODUCTLINE alphabetically or by SALES descending if preferred
    # The example target shows no particular order, but let's sort by SALES descending
    result_df = result_df.sort_values(by='SALES', ascending=False).reset_index(drop=True)

    # Write the result to the target CSV file
    target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_59/target_multisource_cot.csv"
    result_df.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
